blocks.text: a) The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural: *Вот столы. — Я вижу столы. Вот книги. — Я вижу книги.* b) The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural: *Это студенты и студентки. — Здесь нет студентов и студенток. — Я знаю студентов и студенток.*

For the dative and the prepositional plural there are two kinds of endings for each case: -ам, -ами, -ах after a hard, a sibilant or a guttural consonant; -ям, -ями, -ях after a soft consonant, a «ь» or a vowel. The formation of these cases does not depend upon the gender of the noun, but only upon the sound preceding the ending.

Notes. 1) Three nouns: люди, дети and дочери have the instrumental case ending -ьми instead of -ями: людьми, детьми, дочерьми. 2) Masculine and neuter nouns with the irregular plural ending in -ья (стулья, перья, etc.) retain the «ь»: стульям, стульями, о стульях.

Masculine nouns with the irregular nominative plural in -а or -я have the regular declension in all other cases: дома — домов — домам; учителя — учителей — учителям. Hard masculine nouns in -ц have in the genitive the ending -ев if unstressed: немцев, месяцев. The nouns крестьяне, англичане, хозяева and господа have an irregular nominative and an irregular genitive (no ending): крестьян, хозяев, господ; the other cases are regular: крестьянам, хозяевам, господам.
The preposition по is also used in time expressions with the dative plural of nouns in the meaning "on", "in" (repeatedly): *по четвергам* — on Thursdays; *по утрам* — in the mornings.
